group_assessment.weighting: A molecular carcinogenesis group (the senior author led the first WWOX loss-of-heterozygosity work in breast cancer) studying WWOX as a tumour suppressor in Wilms' tumour; primary for the gene in cancer, not for biallelic-loss neurological disease. Observation (mRNA levels, methylation calls, LOH rates) is weighted above interpretation (WWOX involved in carcinogenesis, in apoptosis and ErbB4 signalling), which rests on 23 tumours without an adjacent normal comparator.

entries.proposition: Table I (text layer and page render): observed hemizygosity 30.4% (D16S3096, intron 8) and 6.7% (D16S518, intron 1); population homozygosity 26% and 17%; predicted loss of heterozygosity 4.4% and 0. The headline '30.4% LOH' is the observed hemizygosity, not the predicted LOH; about one of 23 tumours (4.4%) is a predicted LOH at intron 8. The paper's own conclusion that LOH 'did not influence' expression is therefore about a very small group.

entries.proposition: Figure 1 (page 3 render, 150 dpi): western blot of six tumours, samples 3, 15 and 88 with low relative mRNA (1.48, 0.21, 0.96) and 89, 91, 92 with high (58.3, 36.5, 49.2). Samples 3 and 15 show visible WWOX bands, sample 88 shows none, samples 89 and 91 show bands of moderate intensity and sample 92 a strong band beside a nearly absent GAPDH band. A 40- to 280-fold difference in mRNA is not matched by a comparable protein difference; the blot validates direction at best and not magnitude.

entries.proposition: Promoter methylation lowers WWOX expression in the two assayed regions: mean relative expression 15.94 unmethylated versus 4.01 methylated (P = 0.036) for the first region, and 14.92 versus 0.83 (P = 0.0037) for the second, with methylation in 13.64% and 8.7% of tumours (about 3 and 2 tumours); no heterozygous-loss effect; correlations with the clinical factors age, stage and risk are null.
